scope: Same complete 81-path review scope, all 112 obligations and ten shared scopes.

semantic_notes: The equal-key range256 counterexample has distinct payloads but comparator false, actual exercise131585 and literal132353, both exceeding their distinct-key binary-log constants32 and64 at size256.

InsertionRun and sortRun remain arbitrary-payload and arbitrary decidable-relation operations. Their returned values are exactly orderedInsert/insertionSort, and the sort recurrence charges the actual insertion into the returned sorted tail.

Insertion costs lie in[1,n+1], with head/all-related cost1 and all-unrelated cost n+1. Sort cost is at least2*n+1, at most(n+1)*(n+2)/2 using Nat division, and at most(n+1)^2. Pairwise r gives exact2*n+1; Pairwise not-r gives exact doubled triangular cost without extra order laws; reverse range realizes the upper bound.
The stability theorem separately requires a key linear preorder, decidable key comparison and equality, without payload equality. No stability is inferred from value equality alone.

MapRun returns the actual mapped values and costs sum of callback charges plus length+1. Its constant-callback specialization is(c+1)*length+1. FilterRun retains the predicate callback charge and recursive charge in both Boolean branches, with actual filter value and the same sum formula.

FilterRun exact and constant-cost statements account for every predicate call, and filter cost equals map cost for the same measured predicate. Take/drop preserve their actual list values with min(k,length)+1 calls; running them separately returns the fused split value at twice its call cost.

LookupRun returns Option with no Inhabited or equality requirement, equals safe list lookup, and costs min(k,length)+1. Valid-index specialization retains the bound proof and returns Some of the actual indexed element with k+1 calls.

ListMerge run, comparison and entry interfaces remain law-free for arbitrary Boolean comparators. Empty cases preserve values with(0 comparisons,1 entry); each nonempty step adds(1,1) to exactly the selected recursive branch, and both nonempty lists imply at least one comparison.
TopDownSorting comparisons are a separate Nat observation; empty and singleton measured runs have zero comparison cost. These are not operational-cost claims.

Ordered-insertion Pairwise extraction is law-free; its equivalence requires totality and transitivity. Filter-negative insertion removes only the rejected new element with no order assumption, while filter-positive commutation retains transitivity and Pairwise input. QuickSortBy recursion keeps two complementary filters and left-output ++ [pivot] ++ right-output.
